title: Sabri and the Borrowed Faces
logline: Sabri wears a hundred masks until Wisal asks to see the one beneath.
story: A hundred faces hung by the door, and Sabri, for all of memory, keeper of old stories, wore a different one for every visitor. Then Wisal, who was union with the beloved, asked a single quiet question: which face do you wear when no one is watching? Sabri had no answer, and that silence was more frightening than any crowd. So Sabri began, slowly, to set the masks down one by one, and found beneath them not emptiness but a plain, unguarded face. It was the only face anyone had ever truly wanted to meet.
moral: The self you hide in order to be loved is the very self that love was looking for.
